text:
maya: Hit a nasty race in the Async Python SDK around auth refresh + httpx retries. Two concurrent requests both get 401 and both kick off refresh; the retry path reuses a prepared request so it resends stale Authorization header. Happening in FastAPI background tasks and our integration suite. Anyone seen similar?

sam: Oof, can you share a tiny repro + logs?

maya: Yep. Super trimmed example below: 

```py
from contextvars import ContextVar
import httpx
import asyncio

_token = ContextVar('token', default=None)
async def refresh_token():
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    return 'tok-' + str(asyncio.get_event_loop().time())

async def auth_hook(request):
    t = _token.get()
    if not t:
        t = await refresh_token()
        _token.set(t)
    request.headers['authorization'] = f'Bearer {t}'
    return request

client = httpx.AsyncClient(event_hooks={'request': [auth_hook]})
```

maya: Logs show two refreshes and then a retry that still uses the old header: 

```
INFO refresh start
INFO refresh success tokA
WARN 401 GET /v1/generate
INFO retry attempt 1
WARN 401 GET /v1/generate
INFO refresh start
INFO refresh success tokB
ERROR request ultimately failed
```

sam: Looks like httpx prepares the request once and reuses it for retries, so request hooks don't run again. That would explain stale headers. Also ContextVar propagation can be tricky across tasks.

leo: Two things: (1) dedupe refreshes with an asyncio.Lock or singleflight pattern so only one refresh happens at a time; (2) ensure retries call your auth logic before send instead of reusing a prepared request.

maya: Agreed. I'm thinking of switching auth to a transport-level hook or writing a small AsyncAuth that sets headers at send-time. That way each attempt picks up the latest token. But httpx.Auth is pretty sync-oriented; might need a custom transport shim.

sam: Short-term workaround for our SDK: wrap refresh_token with a per-client lock and make retry logic re-run request hooks. Longer-term, consider moving auth into the transport layer so retries re-add headers.

leo: Also noticed the SDK's typing hurt DX: our Async client type is currently ambiguous and mypy treats it like sync client in a lot of code. We should add an explicit AsyncInferenceClient Protocol and overloads for __aenter__/__aexit__ so `async with` is typed correctly.

maya: I'll draft a regression test that spawns N concurrent requests while expiring the token and assert only one refresh runs and retries observe fresh header. Will also test with FastAPI background tasks to mimic production.

ci-bot: created issue #3772 "async auth + retry race -> stale auth headers"

devex: When you open the PR, mark the new test as flaky in CI until we add the fixture to stabilize timing. Also add a short note to migration docs about ContextVar vs per-client token storage and the recommended pattern (per-client lock + transport auth).

maya: Will open draft PR in a few hours. I'll include both a fix (lock + reapply hooks before retry) and an optional transport shim example in the docs.

sam: For the typing fix I'm happy to pair with leo. Adding AsyncClient Protocol should be a small, safe change.

leo: Thanks, this will help customers using asyncio+httpx a lot.

maya: Thanks all — saved me from chasing phantom 401s. :rocket:
